key_insight: Using the original Miller-Robert-Sommeria framework, the paper shows that generic vorticity fields on a sphere relax to a quadrupole statistical equilibrium, but real turbulent evolution can still form concentrated vortices because mixing barriers prevent full equilibration.
engineering_relevance: This helps CFD surrogate and reduced-order models distinguish between long-time statistical states and dynamically persistent coherent structures in spherical geophysical flows.
method: Compute statistical equilibria from the original MRS theory for a generic initial vorticity field on a sphere
Compare equilibrium macroscopic vorticity/stream-function structure with direct long-term time integration of the vorticity equation
Repeat the equilibrium calculation with planetary vorticity to examine rotation-rate-dependent state transitions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the computed equilibrium matches a quadrupole topology seen in long-term integration, and that increasing angular velocity shifts equilibria from quadrupole to zonally symmetric states.
watch_item: The equilibrium theory does not capture concentrated vortices observed in time integration, so models must account for mixing barriers and incomplete relaxation.
paper_title: Statistical equilibria of two-dimensional turbulent flows for generic initial vorticity fields on a sphere, calculated on the basis of the original Miller-Robert-Sommeria theory
